title: Sunumlar
canDo: Cleft sentence'larla (It was ... that, What I need is ...) bir bilgiyi öne çıkarabilir, sunum yaparken yönlendirme ifadeleriyle dinleyiciyi yönetebilir, görselleri anlatabilir, soruları profesyonelce cevaplayabilir ve etkili bir sunum metni hazırlayabilirim.

liveClass.title: Üç dakikada fikrim
liveClass.goal: Her öğrenci okulunu, işini ya da şehrini iyileştirecek bir fikri 3 dakikalık bir sunumla anlatır. Sınıf en ikna edici sunumu oylar.

lessons.title: Asıl önemli olan
lessons.goal: It-cleft (It was ... that / who) yapısıyla bir bilgiyi öne çıkarabilir ve bir yanlış anlamayı düzeltebilirim.

learn.explanation:
**Cleft sentence** ("bölünmüş cümle"), bir cümleyi ikiye bölerek **bir bilgiyi öne çıkarır**.

**It + be + [vurgulanan kısım] + that / who + [cümlenin geri kalanı]**

**Normal cümle:** *The supplier caused the delay last week.*

| Vurgulanan | It-cleft |
|---|---|
| Kim? | **It was the supplier that / who** caused the delay. |
| Ne? | **It was the delay that** worried us. |
| Ne zaman? | **It was last week that** the delay happened. |
| Nerede? | **It was in Izmir that** we met. |
| Neden? | **It was because of the rain that** we cancelled. |

**En güçlü kullanım: düzeltme (contrast)**

- ***It wasn't** the design team **that** caused the delay. **It was** the supplier.*
- ***It's not** money **that** we need, **it's** time.*

**Kurallar:**

- Kişi için **who** ya da **that**; diğerleri için **that**.
- **be** fiilinin zamanı genellikle cümlenin zamanına uyar: *It **was** ... that ...* (geçmiş) / *It **is** ... that ...* (şimdi)
- **It was only when / only after ... that ...** = ancak ... -ince: *It was only last Thursday that we discovered it.*

**Konuşmada:** Vurgulanan kelime **yüksek tonla** söylenir.

examples.en: It was my grandmother who taught me to cook.
It isn't the price that worries me, it's the quality.
It was only when I moved abroad that I learned to appreciate home.
examples.tr: Evin değerini ancak yurt dışına taşındığımda anladım.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede vurgu, vurgulanan öğeyi fiilin hemen önüne koyarak yapılır: "Gecikmeye tedarikçi neden oldu" (vurgu: tedarikçi). İngilizcede kelime sırası sabit olduğu için bu iş için "It was the supplier that..." yapısı kullanılır. Türkçedeki "-an/-en ... -dir" yapısı da ("Bana yemek yapmayı öğreten büyükannemdi") it-cleft'e çok yakındır; çeviri yaparken bu yapıyı düşünün.

options: It was Ali who called me.

lessons.title: İhtiyacımız olan şey
lessons.goal: Wh-cleft (What I need is ..., What happened was ...) yapısıyla bir fikri ya da olayı dramatik bir şekilde sunabilirim.

discover.title: Bir girişimcinin sunumu
discover.body:
Good afternoon, everyone.

What I'd like to talk about today is food waste. What surprised me most when I started researching this topic was that nearly a third of all the food we produce is never eaten.

So what did we do? What we did was to create an app that connects restaurants with people who want to buy their leftover food at a lower price.

What happened next was amazing. In just six months, more than 200 restaurants joined.

What we need now is investment, so that we can expand to other cities. And what I'm asking you for today is not just money. What I really want is partners who care about this problem as much as we do.

options: It connects restaurants with people who buy leftover food.
questions.explanation: "connects restaurants with people who want to buy their leftover food"

questions.prompt: What does the speaker really want?
options: Partners who care about the problem
questions.explanation: "What I really want is partners who care about this problem"

learn.explanation:
**Wh-cleft (pseudo-cleft):** *What* + özne + fiil + **is / was** + [vurgulanan bilgi]

Dinleyicinin dikkatini **asıl bilgiye** çekmek için "merak" yaratır.

| Normal | Wh-cleft |
|---|---|
| We need investment. | **What we need is** investment. |
| The result surprised me. | **What surprised me was** the result. |
| I'd like to talk about food waste. | **What I'd like to talk about is** food waste. |

**Eylemi vurgulamak: What ... do / did + is / was + (to) + fiil**

| Normal | Wh-cleft |
|---|---|
| We created an app. | **What we did was (to) create** an app. |
| You should rest. | **What you should do is rest.** |

**Olayı vurgulamak: What happened was (that) ...**

- ***What happened was that** the server crashed.*

**Ters sıralama da mümkün:**

- *Investment **is what we need**.* (daha vurgulu sonuç)
- *That's **what I mean**.*

**Dikkat:**

- **What** = the thing(s) that; ~~The thing what~~ ✗
- Vurgulanan kısım çoğul olsa bile genellikle **is** kullanılır: *What we need **is** more volunteers.*

examples.en: What I love about this city is the food.
What you need to do is talk to your manager.
What happened was that we missed the last train.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "Bize lazım olan şey yatırım" ya da "Olan şuydu: ..." yapıları wh-cleft'e çok benzer ve doğal bir şekilde kullanılır. İngilizcede de sunumlarda ve tartışmalarda çok yaygındır. Türkçe konuşanların sık yaptığı hata, "The thing what" ya da "What we need, it is" gibi fazladan kelimeler eklemektir. "What we need is..." yapısı tek başına yeterlidir.

options: What we need it is more time.
What we need is more time.
The thing what I love is music.
What we did was to call the police.
What we called was the police.

task.prompt: Bir sorunu ve çözümünüzü yatırımcılara sunuyormuş gibi kısa bir "pitch" yapın (1 dakika). En az 5 wh-cleft kullanın: What I'd like to talk about is ..., What surprised me was ..., What we did was (to) ..., What happened was ..., What we need is ...
task.modelAnswer: Good morning. What I'd like to talk about today is loneliness among older people. What surprised me when I started volunteering was how many elderly people go days without speaking to anyone. So what we did was to create a programme that matches university students with older neighbours for a weekly coffee. What happened next was wonderful: both groups said they felt happier. What we need now is funding to bring this programme to every neighbourhood in the city.

learn.explanation:
Wh-cleft'e benzer, ama **what** yerine bir isim kullanan yapılar:

| Yapı | Anlam | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **All** + özne + fiil + **is** | tek ... şey | **All I want is** a website that works. |
| **The reason (why)** ... **is that** | ... -in nedeni ... | **The reason (why)** it failed **is that** nobody tested it. |
| **The thing (that)** ... **is** | ... şey | **The thing that** annoys me **is** the noise. |
| **The person who** ... **is** | ... kişi | **The person who** helped me most **was** my coach. |
| **The place where** ... **is** | ... yer | **The place where** I feel happiest **is** the sea. |
| **The time when** ... **was** | ... zaman | **The time when** I felt proudest **was** ... |
| **The first / last / only thing** ... **is** | ilk / son / tek şey | **The only thing** I regret **is** not travelling more. |

**All I did was + (to) + fiil:**

- ***All I did was** ask a question!* (Sadece bir soru sordum! → savunma)

**Dikkat:**

- ~~The reason is because~~ → **The reason is that** (resmî dilde "because" tekrarı hatalı kabul edilir)
- **All** = the only thing: ~~All what I want~~ ✗ → **All I want** ✓

examples.en: All I need is a good night's sleep.
examples.tr: Tek ihtiyacım güzel bir gece uykusu.

examples.en: The reason I'm calling is that I have a question about my bill.
examples.tr: Aramamın nedeni faturamla ilgili bir sorum olması.

examples.en: The only thing I regret is not learning English earlier.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçedeki "Tek istediğim...", "... -mesinin sebebi ...", "Beni en çok rahatsız eden şey ..." yapıları bu kalıplarla birebir örtüşür. Türkçe konuşanların en sık hatası "All what I want" demektir (Türkçedeki "bütün istediğim şey"den); doğrusu "All I want". Bir diğer yaygın hata "The reason is because..."; resmî İngilizcede "The reason is that..." tercih edilir.

options: All what I want is peace.
The reason is because it's expensive.
The reason is that it's expensive.

task.modelAnswer: All I need to be happy is good food and good friends. The thing that annoys me most is people who are always late. The person who has influenced me most is my aunt, who travelled the world on her own. The place where I feel most at home is my grandparents' village. lessons.title: Sunumu yönetmek
lessons.goal: Yönlendirme ifadeleri (signposting), görsel anlatım ve soru-cevap kalıplarıyla bir sunumu profesyonelce yönetebilirim.

discover.title: Sunumdan bir bölüm
discover.body:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming. My name is Tuba Arıkan, and I'm the marketing manager.

Today, I'd like to talk about our new strategy for young customers. I've divided my presentation into three parts. First, I'll look at the current situation. Then, I'll present our research. And finally, I'll suggest some next steps. Please feel free to interrupt if you have any questions.

So, let's start with the current situation. As you can see from this chart, sales to customers under 25 have fallen steadily over the last two years.

That brings me to my second point: why? Let me illustrate this with a quote from one of our focus groups: "Your brand feels like something my parents would buy."

Moving on to my final point...

[Later]

That's a very good question. If I understand correctly, you're asking whether the new strategy will affect older customers. I'm glad you asked that...

questions.prompt: How many parts does the presentation have?

options: Sales to young customers have fallen.
questions.explanation: "sales to customers under 25 have fallen steadily"

learn.explanation:
**Sunumun bölümleri ve kalıplar:**

| Bölüm | Kalıplar |
|---|---|
| **Açılış** | *Good morning, and thank you for coming.* / *I'd like to talk to you about ...* / *The purpose of this presentation is to ...* |
| **Plan** | *I've divided my presentation into three parts.* / *First, I'll ... Then, ... Finally, ...* |
| **Başlama** | *So, let's start with ...* / *I'd like to begin by ...* |
| **Geçiş** | *Moving on to ...* / *That brings me to my next point.* / *Let's now turn to ...* |
| **Örnek** | *Let me illustrate this with an example.* / *To give you an idea, ...* |
| **Vurgu** | *I'd like to highlight ...* / *What's really important here is ...* / *It's worth bearing in mind that ...* |
| **Konu dışı** | *Sorry, I'm digressing. Back to ...* |
| **Özet / kapanış** | *To sum up, ...* / *In a nutshell, ...* / *I'd like to finish by ...* / *Thank you for your attention.* |

**Görselleri anlatmak:**

- *As you can see from this chart / on this slide, ...*
- *This graph shows / illustrates ...*
- *If you look at the figures on the left, ...*
- *I'd like to draw your attention to ...*

**Soru-cevap:**

| Durum | Kalıp |
|---|---|
| Zaman kazanmak | *That's a very good question.* / *I'm glad you asked that.* |
| Soruyu kontrol etmek | *If I understand correctly, you're asking ...* |
| Cevabı bilmiyorsanız | *I'm afraid I don't have that information right now, but I'll find out and get back to you.* |
| Kapsam dışıysa | *That's slightly outside the scope of today's presentation, but ...* |

examples.en: That brings me to my next point.
examples.tr: Bu beni bir sonraki noktama getiriyor.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçe sunumlarda geçişler genellikle "Şimdi ...'a geçelim" gibi tek bir kalıpla yapılır. İngilizce sunumlarda çeşitli yönlendirme ifadeleri dinleyicinin "haritayı" kaybetmemesini sağlar ve konuşmacıyı çok daha profesyonel gösterir. Bilmediğiniz bir soruya cevap uydurmak yerine "I'll get back to you" demek, İngilizce iş kültüründe gayet kabul görür.

options: I'm afraid I don't have that information, but I'll get back to you.

lessons.title: Sunum metni
lessons.goal: Cleft sentence'lar, yönlendirme dili ve etkili bir yapıyla dinleyiciyi etkileyen bir sunum metni yazabilirim.

discover.title: Kısa bir konuşmanın metni: Neden okumalıyız?
discover.body:
Good evening.

Let me start with a question. When was the last time you read a book, not on a screen, just a book, for more than an hour?

For most of us, it's been a while. And that's what I want to talk about tonight.

I'd like to make three points. First, why reading matters. Second, why we've stopped. And third, what we can do about it.

So, why does reading matter? It isn't just about information. What reading really gives us is empathy. When we read a novel, we live inside someone else's mind. Studies suggest that people who read fiction regularly are better at understanding other people's feelings.

That brings me to my second point. Why have we stopped? The reason, I think, is not that we've lost interest. It's that our attention is constantly being taken by our phones.

So what can we do? All it takes is twenty minutes a day. Leave your phone in another room. Pick up a book. That's it.

To sum up: reading makes us more human. It was a book that changed my life when I was fifteen. Maybe tonight, one will change yours.

Thank you.

questions.prompt: What does reading really give us, according to the speaker?
questions.explanation: "What reading really gives us is empathy."

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's practical suggestion?
options: Read for twenty minutes a day without your phone.
questions.explanation: "All it takes is twenty minutes a day. Leave your phone in another room."

learn.explanation:
**Etkili bir sunum metninin yapısı:**

| Bölüm | Teknik | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **Kanca (hook)** | Soru, şaşırtıcı bir rakam, kısa bir hikâye | *When was the last time you ...?* |
| **Konu ve plan** | Ne anlatacağınızı söyleyin | *I'd like to make three points.* |
| **Gelişme** | Her bölüm bir mesaj + kanıt/örnek | *What reading really gives us is empathy.* |
| **Geçişler** | Signposting | *That brings me to my second point.* |
| **Çağrı** | Dinleyiciden somut bir eylem | *All it takes is twenty minutes a day.* |
| **Kapanış** | Özet + başa dönüş + güçlü son | *Maybe tonight, one will change yours.* |

**Konuşma için yazmak ≠ okumak için yazmak:**

- **Kısa cümleler** kullanın; dinleyici geri dönüp okuyamaz.
- **Tekrar** edin: Ana mesajı başta, ortada ve sonda söyleyin.
- **Cleft sentence**'larla en önemli bilgiyi **cümlenin sonuna** (dinleyicinin dikkatinin en yüksek olduğu yere) koyun: *What we need is **courage**.*
- **Doğrudan hitap:** *you, we, us*
- **Duraklama** yerleri bırakın (yazıda yeni satır).

**Cleft sentence'ların sunumdaki gücü:** Vurgulanan bilgiyi **beklenti yaratarak** sunarlar: *The reason I'm here tonight is ... [duraklama] ... you.*

examples.en: Let me start with a question.
What I want you to remember is this: small changes matter.
examples.tr: Hatırlamanızı istediğim şey şu: küçük değişiklikler önemlidir.

examples.tr: Her şeyi değiştiren tek bir konuşmaydı.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçe sunumlarda giriş bölümü bazen uzun teşekkürler ve resmî hitaplarla geçer. İngilizce sunum kültüründe ise ilk 30 saniye dinleyicinin dikkatini çekmek için çok değerlidir: bir soru, bir hikâye ya da şaşırtıcı bir bilgiyle başlamak beklenir. Teşekkürler kısa tutulur ve genellikle sona bırakılır.

practice.audioText: Imagine a city with no cars. No traffic, no noise, no pollution. Sounds impossible? It isn't. What I'd like to show you tonight is how three European cities did exactly that, and what we can learn from them.

task.prompt: TED tarzı 3–4 dakikalık bir konuşmanın metnini yazın (250–300 kelime). Konu: Hayatınızda önemli bulduğunuz bir fikir ya da alışkanlık (yürüyüş, gönüllülük, dil öğrenmek, erken kalkmak, vb.). Bir kancayla başlayın, planınızı söyleyin, en az 4 farklı cleft sentence (It was ... that, What ... is, The reason ... is that, All ... is) ve en az 3 yönlendirme ifadesi kullanın; dinleyiciye somut bir çağrıyla ve güçlü bir kapanışla bitirin. Konuşma için yazın: kısa cümleler, doğrudan hitap.
task.modelAnswer:
Good evening.

Raise your hand if you've ever said, "I'm not good at languages."

Keep it up if you still believe that.

I used to. For years, I was sure I didn't have "the gift". And that's what I want to talk about tonight: the myth of the language gift.

I'd like to make three points. First, why the myth exists. Second, what really makes people successful. And finally, what you can do, starting tomorrow.

So, let's start with the myth. Why do so many of us believe it? The reason, I think, is that we compare ourselves with children. Children seem to learn effortlessly. But what we forget is that a child hears their language for thousands of hours before they say a full sentence.

That brings me to my second point. What makes successful language learners different? It isn't talent. It's time and habit. In every study I've read, the best learners are not the most gifted. They're the most consistent.

It was a simple decision that changed everything for me. I stopped studying for three hours on Sunday, and I started studying for fifteen minutes every single day.

So, what can you do? All you need is fifteen minutes. A podcast on the bus. Five new words before bed. One conversation a week.

To sum up: there's no such thing as "not good at languages". There's only "not enough practice yet".

Tomorrow morning, give English your first fifteen minutes. And in a year, I'd love to hear what you say then.

Thank you.

questions.prompt: Şirketinize, okulunuza ya da belediyenize bir öneri sunduğunuz kısa bir sunum metni yazın (220–270 kelime). Kancayla başlayın, planı söyleyin, sorunu ve çözümünüzü anlatın, bir görsele atıfta bulunun (As you can see ...), en az 4 cleft sentence ve en az 4 yönlendirme ifadesi kullanın ve bir çağrıyla bitirin.
questions.modelAnswer:
Good morning, everyone.

Let me start with a number: forty-five. That's how many minutes the average employee in our building spends every day looking for a parking space, waiting for the lift or queuing for lunch.

What I'd like to talk about today is how we can win back that time. I've divided my presentation into three parts: the problem, our solution and the next steps.

So, let's begin with the problem. As you can see from this chart, our staff numbers have doubled in five years, but our building hasn't changed. It isn't laziness that is making people late for meetings. It's the building itself.

That brings me to our solution. What we're proposing is a simple three-step plan. First, a flexible start time between eight and ten, so that not everyone arrives at once. Second, an online system for booking parking spaces. And third, a second lunch break at one thirty.

The reason we believe this will work is that two of our partner companies have already tried it. In both cases, staff satisfaction rose by more than twenty percent.

Moving on to the next steps. All we need from you today is approval for a three-month trial. It would cost almost nothing, and if it doesn't work, we can simply go back to the current system.

To sum up: forty-five minutes a day is almost four hours a week. Imagine what our team could do with that time.

Thank you. I'm happy to take any questions.
